title: The Poisoned Professor
subtitle: A departmental meeting, and one cup that mattered
briefing: Professor Alan Reeve collapses forty minutes after a departmental meeting and is taken to hospital in a critical condition. Toxicology finds a cardiac drug in his system at several times the therapeutic dose. He does not take that drug. Six people were in the room, the coffee was poured from a shared pot, and the cups were laid out in advance with names on them.
solution: Vikram Rao had access to the departmental drug cabinet as the departmental safety officer, and had learned that Reeve intended to name him in a research misconduct report the following week. He dosed the cup laid out at Reeve's place before the meeting began. The medication bottle found in Reeve's office was his own prescription and had nothing to do with it.

topics.before_meeting: where they were before the meeting

suspects.name: Dr Vikram Rao
suspects.motive: Was about to be named in a research misconduct report.

statements.question: Where were you before the meeting?
statements.text: In my office, marking. I came in at two thirty-five with everyone else.

statements.question: Who laid the cups out?
statements.text: The department secretary, as always. It is not a task any of us would want.

statements.question: Who has access to the drug cabinet?
statements.text: It is a shared key. Half the department could sign it out.

statements.question: Were you aware of a misconduct report?
statements.text: This is the first I have heard of any report.

suspects.name: Dr Helen Vance
suspects.motive: Competing with Reeve for the same research funding.

statements.question: Where were you before the meeting?
statements.text: Setting up the room from about two twenty. I was in and out.

statements.question: Who laid the cups out?
statements.text: Priya did, before I got there. They were already on the side table.

statements.question: Do you have drug cabinet access?
statements.text: No. I have not signed that key out in four years.

statements.question: Were you aware of a misconduct report?
statements.text: Alan mentioned he was preparing something. He did not say against whom.

suspects.name: Priya Raman
suspects.motive: Was passed over for a permanent contract that Reeve blocked.

statements.question: Where were you before the meeting?
statements.text: In the seminar room from two fifteen, laying out the cups and the agenda.

statements.question: Who laid the cups out?
statements.text: I did. Names on the saucers, the way Professor Reeve insists.

statements.question: Do you have drug cabinet access?
statements.text: Absolutely not. I would not know where it is kept.

statements.question: Were you aware of a misconduct report?
statements.text: No, and I would have typed it if there were one.

suspects.name: Dr Callum Bright
suspects.motive: Reeve rejected his promotion case twice.

statements.question: Where were you before the meeting?
statements.text: In the corridor on the phone until about two thirty-eight.

statements.question: Who laid the cups out?
statements.text: Priya. She always does.

statements.question: Do you have drug cabinet access?
statements.text: I have signed the key out, yes. For a third year practical, in October.

statements.question: Were you aware of a misconduct report?
statements.text: Everyone knew he was writing one. Nobody knew who it named.

suspects.name: Dr Nadia Okafor
suspects.motive: Her contract depended on Reeve's grant renewal.

statements.question: Where were you before the meeting?
statements.text: In the lab until two thirty-six. The instrument log will show it.

statements.question: Who laid the cups out?
statements.text: Priya. I saw her carrying the tray in.

statements.question: Do you have drug cabinet access?
statements.text: No. Postdocs are not on that list.

statements.question: Were you aware of a misconduct report?
statements.text: Alan asked me to check a dataset for him last month. He was very careful about who saw it.

locations.name: Seminar Room
locations.description: Twelve chairs, a side table with six cups, and a window that does not open.

searchables.label: Examine Professor Reeve's cup
searchables.flavour: A faint residue at the base, below the coffee line.

searchables.label: Test the coffee pot
searchables.flavour: Clean. Whatever it was, it was not in the pot.

locations.name: Reeve's Office
locations.description: Books to the ceiling and a desk that has not been tidied in a decade.

searchables.label: Examine the medication bottle
searchables.flavour: A prescription in his own name.

searchables.label: Go through the waste bin
searchables.flavour: A torn envelope with a departmental frank.

locations.name: Drug Cabinet Store
locations.description: A locked steel cabinet, a signing-out book, and a key nobody guards properly.

searchables.label: Read the signing-out register
searchables.flavour: One entry the week before, in a hurried hand.

searchables.label: Count the stock
searchables.flavour: The count is short by more than the register admits.

locations.name: Teaching Laboratory
locations.description: Benches, an instrument log, and a swipe reader on the door.

searchables.label: Check the glove bin
searchables.flavour: A pair of gloves pushed to the bottom, inside out.

locations.name: Cafeteria
locations.description: Where four of the six were seen at various points that afternoon.

searchables.label: Check the till receipts
searchables.flavour: Times, to the second, and no ambiguity.

evidence.name: Residue in the cup
evidence.description: A cardiac drug residue at the base of the cup laid at Reeve's place.

evidence.name: Clean coffee pot
evidence.description: The shared pot tests clear. The dose went into one cup only.

evidence.name: Named place cards
evidence.description: Cups were laid at named places, so the target was chosen in advance.

evidence.name: Medication bottle
evidence.description: A bottle of Reeve's own prescription, unrelated to the drug found.

evidence.name: Cabinet register entry
evidence.description: The cabinet key was signed out the previous week by V. Rao.

evidence.name: Short stock count
evidence.description: The cabinet holds less of the drug than the register accounts for.

evidence.name: Door swipe records
evidence.description: Vikram entered the seminar room at 2:21 PM, fourteen minutes before he claims.

evidence.name: Discarded gloves
evidence.description: A pair of gloves in the lab bin, inside out, with cabinet dust on them.

evidence.name: Draft misconduct report
evidence.description: An unsigned draft naming a senior member of the department.

evidence.name: Torn internal envelope
evidence.description: A departmental envelope addressed to Dr V. Rao, opened and discarded.

evidence.name: Cafeteria receipt
evidence.description: Priya was at the till at 2:19 PM, before the room was laid out.

evidence.name: Named page of the report
evidence.description: The draft's second page names Vikram Rao directly.

timeline.text: Priya begins laying out the seminar room.
Priya is recorded at the cafeteria till.
A swipe records entry to the seminar room.
The meeting begins. Coffee is poured.
Professor Reeve collapses in the corridor.

hints: The pot is clean. Ask what that tells you about when the dose was added.
One person's account of their own arrival time can be checked against a door reader.
Find out who the report was going to name.
